page: Amazon Web Services r8i.large is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2163.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression (34.33 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.25 GB/sec). However, due to its low core count of 1 physical core, multi-core performance is limited, as reflected in a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2725.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core CPU performance rating. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 20.69 GB/sec and a write speed of 17.1 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also fall into lower performance tiers, while LLM text generation for a small 135M model achieves an average speed of 98.37 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i.large offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on modern DDR5 hardware, making it a resource-dense entry point for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The primary tradeoff is the limited multi-core compute scaling. This instance is best suited for low-scale memory-intensive applications, single-threaded data processing tasks, lightweight caching layers, or development environments mimicking larger memory-optimized production systems.
